mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and economic activity improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST increases for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate fiscal stimulus.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: low interest rate environment with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 1% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real final sales of domestic product (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where RSAFS increases for two consecutive months.
